facts.text: Cobalt was incorporated in 1952 and its name comes from the region's sporadic cobalt mining history.
The village sits just one mile west of Fredericktown, on the historic Mine La Motte-Fredericktown mining district of the Ozark Plateau.
In the late 1950s, the Madison Mine employed about 250 workers, paying wages higher than local factory jobs, boosting the nearby downtown economy.
Lead mining has shaped the area since the early 18th century, drawing pioneers to surface galena deposits and creating a mix of farming and extractive communities.
Cobalt lies within Missouri's Lead Belt, a region known for rolling hills, forests, and streams typical of the Ozark Plateau.
The village's economy today includes health care, accommodation, manufacturing, and mining, reflecting its extractive heritage.
